work_order.approach:
One work order, five edits, each closing one finding with the smallest change that removes the problem rather than documenting it.

For finding 1 I take the reviewer's first option (pass the effective value from the caller) over the second (export a type or assertion tying a Weekly intervals array to its endDate). The type/assertion option encodes the invariant the reviewer is worried about — that intervals is derived from endDate — which is exactly the coupling to remove; a branded array type would make a future caller satisfy a constraint rather than stop depending on it. Passing the value is also smaller: recalculate already receives endDate, and both call sites already compute effectiveEndDate two lines earlier for their query bound (custom-spreadsheet.ts:121, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:59). So the prop swaps endDate+interval+firstDayOfWeekIdx for effectiveEndDate, and recalculate stops calling getEffectiveEndDate and stops importing it. Net: three props out, one in, one import gone, and the invariant disappears rather than being documented.

I prototyped this exact change, ran `yarn typecheck` (all workspaces green) and the reports suite (421 tests green), then reverted it. The implementer is writing the same change; the prototype exists to prove the shape compiles and that the green suite is what this change is expected to preserve.

For finding 5 I take the reviewer's primary fix (use getByText at both sites, keep getHeader for the yearly case) over the alternative (keep the DOM walk and rename the helper), and I verified it passes before writing it down. The reviewer's secondary point stands and I am folding it in: the pair at :130-157 exists to prove the pref reaches the header, so the helper's doc comment must be narrowed to say it is for reading the header node itself — which after this change is only the yearly case.

For finding 4 I compress both copies to one sentence rather than deleting both. The reviewer offered three options; deleting both is tempting because the budgeted-path test at custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:392-425 already carries the premise as executable evidence, but that test proves the premise holds, not why the guard is budgeted-only — a reader at the guard is the one who needs the sentence. One sentence, identical in both files, is not the reviewer's complaint: the complaint is seven lines of reasoning the helper's JSDoc already carries. The premise itself (budget rows are month-keyed, weekly buckets are week-start-keyed) stays, compressed, because it is the part a reader cannot see in the two lines of code below the comment.

ON THE TWO CORRECTIONS TO v1's CRITERIA. These change no code — they change what QA is told to look at.

For AC-1 I take the reviewer's option (b), the drill-down, and I verified it renders rather than assuming it. The column label the table and graph print is the interval START; intervalEndDate is never rendered. It IS observable one click away: clicking a cell in the final weekly column calls showActivity with endDate = that bucket's intervalEndDate, which for a weekly report becomes a `date lte` filterCondition (showActivity.ts, `isDateOp = interval === 'Weekly'`), navigates to /accounts, and is rendered by FilterExpression as a pill reading 'date is less than or equals <date>'. I rendered the real conditions through the real FiltersStack and read that text. So AC-1 now checks two things a browser can actually show: the header range (ReportSummary.tsx:92-96 renders `startDate to effectiveEndDate`, and it changes if the threading is wrong) and the drill-down bound read off the filter pill on /accounts. The header is rendered in the sidebar's summary pane, which requires the 'Show Summary' toggle in the report topbar — I have written that into how_to_verify so QA does not go looking for a header that is switched off by default (viewSummary defaults to false, CustomReport.tsx:159).

For the first-day-of-week step I switch To to 2026-09-28 and state the shift as an equality, computed with the repo's own helpers under a pinned currentDay. I also give QA a rule and an invariant rather than only a date, so the check survives QA picking a different To: for a Weekly report whose final week has fully elapsed, changing first day of week from Sunday to Monday moves the final column's label forward by exactly one day and moves the header's end forward by exactly one day, and the two agree with each other. The worked example (To = 2026-09-28) gives the exact strings. I verified the day arithmetic is a real property and not a coincidence of one date: 2026-09-28 is a Monday, so weekFromDate(.., '1') = 2026-09-28 and getWeekEnd(.., '1') = 2026-10-04, while weekFromDate(.., '0') = 2026-09-27 and getWeekEnd(.., '0') = 2026-10-03 — one day on each side.

No new dependency, no new abstraction, no behaviour change anywhere. Every criterion that can be checked in a browser is one that checks the app still behaves as it did on HEAD.

Adding a test for a third caller of recalculate, or for a Weekly intervals array not derived from endDate. The change removes that dependency rather than defending against it, so such a test would assert a state the code can no longer reach.
qa_script: Boot the app (yarn start, port 3001), open the initial setup screen and choose 'View demo' — the empty budget will not exercise a weekly report with a final week in progress.

Reports -> a report (Net Worth or Spending). In the sidebar set Interval to Weekly and Mode to Time. In the report topbar click 'Show Summary' so the date-range header is on screen — it is off by default, and a QA run that skips this will not find the header at all.

Set the To date so the final week has fully elapsed — the Date filters section must be on 'Static' for the From/To pickers to appear (ReportSidebar renders them only when isDateStatic is true). If today is 2026-10-04, pick To = 2026-09-27. Read the summary header range: it must end at the week's true end (10/03/2026), never at the week start and never before it.

CORRECTED IN v2 — v1 said 'the final column must cover the same days in both' views. Neither view prints a per-column range; the column header is the interval START. Read the end date where it is actually printed: switch to the Data Table view (the Data Table button in the report topbar), click any cell in the FINAL weekly column, and read the date filter pill on the /accounts page you land on. It reads 'date is less than or equals <date>'. That is the final bucket's intervalEndDate and it must be 10/03/2026 for this To date. Click the browser Back to return to the report. Repeat from the graph view if the report is grouped by something other than Interval — the bound must be the same date from either view, which is the pair the grouped-spreadsheet comment exists to protect.

CORRECTED IN v2 — v1 said 'shift by exactly one day' with To = 2026-09-27, which is arithmetically wrong for that date. Use To = 2026-09-28 (a Monday) instead, or state the rule rather than a date: for a weekly report whose final week has fully elapsed, changing the first day of week from Sunday to Monday moves the final column's label forward by exactly one day AND moves the header's end forward by exactly one day, and the two agree. With To = 2026-09-28 the exact strings are: final column label '09/27/2026' -> '09/28/2026', and header '09/28/2026 to 10/03/2026' -> '09/28/2026 to 10/04/2026'. Then repeat the step-4 drill-down: the 'date is less than or equals' pill must likewise move from 10/03/2026 to 10/04/2026. These values were computed with the repo's own getEffectiveEndDate and weekFromDate under a pinned today of 2026-10-09, not by hand.
Switch the interval to Monthly and Daily: the header and the drill-down bound must fall back to the raw end date exactly as they do on the base branch (no week widening).

Open the same report with balance type 'Budgeted' at Weekly interval and confirm no error and no figure change against the base branch. Note that the Budgeted balance type navigates to /budget rather than /accounts on drill-down (showActivity.ts), so the step-4 pill is not available there — check only that nothing errors.
Compare every figure, every column label and every range above against the base branch. Any difference is a regression in a work order whose entire claim is that it changes no behaviour.
residual_risks: QA reads this first: four of the ten acceptance criteria are not browser-observable. Findings 2, 3, 4 and 5 are a stale cross-reference, a dead return field, a duplicated comment and a test-assertion style — none of them changes what a user sees, and no browser can confirm any of them. They are marked verify: test with the specific CI case or the specific grep in how_to_verify. AC-1 and AC-9 are the browser checks, and together they are the only thing that would catch a behaviour change.

A refactor work order with no behavioural acceptance is exactly the shape where a slipped edit goes unnoticed because the visible output is unchanged by design. AC-9 (step through every interval and both first-day-of-week settings, compare to base) and AC-10 (the three CI commands) are the net; if QA skips both, this work order has verified nothing.

The compressed budgeted-path comment is a judgement about how much prose a reader needs, and it is the change most likely to draw a review objection on merge. The full reasoning is recoverable from the reviewer's own evidence and from the test at custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:392-425, so nothing is lost irreversibly if a maintainer wants the longer form back.

The step-4 drill-down is the most stateful thing QA is asked to do in this work order: it needs a wide viewport, Group by left off Interval, the Data Table view, and a click that navigates away. Each precondition is named in qa_script step 4 and in risks, because a precondition missed produces a false failure rather than a false pass — QA reports 'the cell does not navigate' and the work order looks broken when it is not.
risks: The largest change is a signature change on an exported function. recalculate is called from exactly three places, all in this repo and all named in files[] — custom-spreadsheet.ts:289, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:113 and :131 — so the blast radius is closed, and TypeScript will catch a missed one at `yarn typecheck` rather than at runtime. I verified the grep for every `recalculate` in the tree: the similarly-named functions in crossover-spreadsheet.ts, calendar-spreadsheet.ts, cash-flow-spreadsheet.tsx and net-worth-spreadsheet.ts are unrelated private helpers.

The nested per-category recalculate call in grouped-spreadsheet.ts is indented four spaces deeper than the outer one and is formatted identically apart from that, which is exactly the shape of an edit an implementer applies to one and misses. Typecheck catches it (the old props would be unknown and effectiveEndDate required), and the three 'weekly grouped report end bound' cases would fail too.

The step-4 drill-down depends on the report being in a state where the cell is clickable: ReportTableRow sets canShowActivity = !isNarrowWidth && groupBy !== 'Interval' && !compact (ReportTableRow.tsx:83). In a narrow viewport, or with Group by set to Interval, the cell does not navigate and the check cannot be run. QA must use a wide viewport and leave Group by on something other than Interval.

The header check depends on the 'Show Summary' toggle being on. viewSummary defaults to false (CustomReport.tsx:159) and the summary pane is also suppressed at narrow widths (`!isNarrowWidth` at :1063), so a run that skips the toggle will report 'no header found'. This is called out in the script and in AC-1's how_to_verify precisely because v1 did not say it.

If the demo budget's transactions do not reach the chosen week, the final column may be empty and the drill-down may list no transactions — the filter PILL is still rendered regardless (FiltersStack renders from filterConditions, not from results), so the date bound remains readable even with an empty list. If QA cannot find a report week with data at all, set the To date to the most recent fully-elapsed week the data does reach and compare against the base branch under the identical setting — the point of the check is equality with base, not a particular date.

No forbidden path is touched. Nothing under .sdlc/**, .github/**, docs/spec/**, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md is in files[]; upcoming-release-notes/ is not forbidden and has direct precedent in clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md.
No host outside env.api_allowlist is involved — this change makes no network call of any kind and adds no dependency.
work_order.root_cause: #76 consolidated the weekly end-date rule out of custom-spreadsheet into the shared getEffectiveEndDate helper, and the consolidation carried three artefacts that the helper's existence made redundant: a cross-reference naming a file that no longer held the rule, a duplicated block of prose that the helper's JSDoc now carries, and a caller that re-derives a value its own caller already computed. The comment/test findings are the same shape — a helper was introduced and the older scaffolding around it was left standing. Separately, v1's own acceptance criteria described UI that does not exist, which is a planning failure rather than a code one and is corrected here.

cases: All fourteen existing cases pass unchanged after the budgetMonths field is removed — in particular 'widens the budgeted query across the month boundary', 'widens the grouped budgeted query the same way', 'moves no figure, because a month-keyed budget row cannot match a weekly bucket' and 'gives the final bucket its full week on the budgeted path too', which are the four that read getBudgetMonths() and so prove the accessor still works once the returned copy is gone.

All three 'weekly grouped report end bound' cases pass unchanged, each of which asserts groupedLast.intervalEndDate equals customLast.intervalEndDate and a literal — these are the cases that would break first if the effectiveEndDate prop were wired into one caller and not the other.

The three 'weekly custom report end bound' cases that pin a literal intervalEndDate ('covers the whole final week once that week has elapsed' to 2026-10-03, 'widens a week-start end date to the week it labels' to 2026-10-03, 'clamps to today while the final week is still in progress' to 2026-10-02) still produce those exact values through the new prop, proving the value is threaded from the caller's existing effectiveEndDate and not recomputed differently.

All nine cases pass, and specifically 'honours a Monday first day of week in the weekly header' and 'stops a Sunday-first week one day earlier than a Monday-first one' now assert via screen.getByText with the strings '09/28/2026 to 10/04/2026' and '09/28/2026 to 10/03/2026' respectively — the same pair of dates, so a failure means the assertion form broke, not that the pref stopped reaching the header.

'collapses a Yearly header that falls inside one year' still passes using getHeader(container).textContent, confirming the helper survives the change for its one remaining caller and that its doc comment now matches what it is used for.

All twenty-two existing cases pass unchanged. No edit is made to this file — it is named because getEffectiveEndDate loses one of its four callers (recalculate.ts) and this test is what proves the helper's own contract survived that.

work_order.understanding:
Issue #78 carries five non-blocking findings the review of PR #76 raised and approved despite. None is a behavioural bug: all five are about code that works but is fragile to read, easy to drift, or dead. I re-checked each against the working tree rather than taking the reviewer's word.

(1) recalculate.ts:99-102 — REPRODUCES. The Weekly branch's final bucket computes intervalEndDate from getEffectiveEndDate(endDate, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx), so the label depends on the caller-supplied invariant that the last element of `intervals` is weekFromDate(endDate). Pre-#76 it computed getWeekEnd(intervalItem) from the bucket's own label and was correct for any intervals array. Both in-tree callers (custom-spreadsheet.ts:166-171, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:104-109) do build intervals via weekRangeInclusive(startDate, endDate, ...), whose last element is weekFromDate(end) (months.ts:292-311 pushes `week` once it equals endWeek), and getWeekEnd is constant within a week — so the equivalence holds today and the nine-line comment at :91-98 records the invariant without enforcing it.

(2) grouped-spreadsheet.ts:56-58 — REPRODUCES. The comment reads 'Same rule as custom-spreadsheet: ...', but #76 deleted the five-line canonical comment at custom-spreadsheet.ts:120-125 and replaced it with a bare call; that file no longer contains the rule. The rule now lives only in the JSDoc at reportRanges.ts:89-103, which neither caller names.

(3) custom-spreadsheet.test.ts budgetMonths — REPRODUCES. Declared in runCustom's return type at :133, produced at :162, and read by nobody: all seven destructurings of runCustom's result omit it, and the four budget assertions all call the module-level getBudgetMonths() accessor instead. Dead field on a helper with eleven other call sites.

(4) the seven-line budgeted-path rationale — REPRODUCES. custom-spreadsheet.ts:144-150 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:82-88 are byte-identical (I re-ran `diff` on the two ranges: IDENTICAL). The work order behind #76 asked for byte-identical comments as a drift guard; the reviewer is right that identical prose in two files is a second copy to maintain, not a guard.

(5) ReportSummary.test.tsx getHeader — REPRODUCES with the reviewer's nuance. The helper's doc comment justifies itself by the yearly case, where the range collapses to a bare year and only exact textContent works. But getHeader is applied at :140 and :156 as well, and those two assert full header strings that are structurally identical to the six the file asserts via screen.getByText — same <Text>, same two expression children (ReportSummary.tsx:92-96). I verified the reviewer's proposed fix rather than assuming it: I converted both to screen.getByText, ran the file, and all 9 tests passed, then restored the file.

Nothing else in the tree reads these. recalculate has exactly two callers — custom-spreadsheet.ts:289 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:113 and :131 (the other functions named recalculate in this repo are unrelated private helpers in their own files). getEffectiveEndDate has four callers: the two factories, ReportSummary.tsx:54, and reportRanges' own test.

ON THE TWO OBJECTIONS AGAINST v1. Both are correct and both are now fixed in the criteria and the QA script rather than argued with.

Objection 1 — v1's AC-1 and qa_script step 4 told QA to read 'the final column's date range in both the graph view and the table view'. No such range is rendered. I re-confirmed the reviewer's grep: intervalEndDate outside tests appears only inside showActivity({...}) arguments (StackedBarGraph.tsx:319, LineGraph.tsx, ReportTableRow.tsx:172) and is never rendered; the visible column label is `date`, the interval START (custom-spreadsheet.ts:263-266, recalculate.ts:104), and both the graph XAxis (dataKey="date") and the table header cell (header.date) render that start label only. v1 asked QA to read a string the app does not print. I take the reviewer's option (b), the drill-down, because it is the only surface where intervalEndEndDate is genuinely observable, and I verified it rather than assuming: I built the exact filterConditions showActivity constructs for a weekly drill-down (startDate = the bucket's intervalStartDate, endDate = the bucket's intervalEndDate, op 'lte', isDateOp true because interval === 'Weekly'), rendered them through the real FiltersStack -> AppliedFilters -> FilterExpression chain, and read the output: 'date is less than or equals 10/03/2026' is on screen, alongside 'date is greater than or equals 09/27/2026'. That text is real, rendered by FilterExpression via mapField/friendlyOp and Value's `formatDate(parseISO(value), dateFormat)` branch. QA clicks the final weekly column in the table view, lands on /accounts, and reads that pill. The header range check is kept alongside it, since ReportSummary.tsx:92-96 does render `startDate to effectiveEndDate` and does change if the threading is wrong.

Objection 2 — v1's qa_script step 5 claimed the final weekly column shifts by exactly one day when the first day of week goes Sunday -> Monday, using To = 2026-09-27. That is arithmetically wrong: 2026-09-27 is a Sunday, so its Sunday-first week runs to 10/03 and its Monday-first week runs 09/21 to 09/27 — a six-day move in both the label and the end. I computed this with the repo's own helpers rather than by hand. Running getEffectiveEndDate and weekFromDate under a pinned currentDay of 2026-10-09 gives: endDate 2026-09-27 fdow=0 label=2026-09-27 effectiveEndDate=2026-10-03; endDate 2026-09-27 fdow=1 label=2026-09-21 effectiveEndDate=2026-09-27; endDate 2026-09-28 fdow=0 label=2026-09-27 effectiveEndDate=2026-10-03; endDate 2026-09-28 fdow=1 label=2026-09-28 effectiveEndDate=2026-10-04. The reviewer is right that the one-day case belongs to 2026-09-28 (a Monday), which is what ReportSummary.test.tsx:133-156 uses. v2 switches the script to To = 2026-09-28 and states the shift as an equality with the strings that date actually produces: label 09/27 -> 09/28, header '09/28/2026 to 10/03/2026' -> '09/28/2026 to 10/04/2026'. I also state the invariant that must hold for any To QA picks instead, so the check does not depend on the exact date.
unknowns: Whether the team considers custom-spreadsheet or grouped-spreadsheet the canonical home for the budgeted-path rationale. The work order has both carry the identical one sentence rather than one pointing at the other, which sidesteps the question — but if the team's preference is a single home with a pointer, that is a one-line change to make deliberately rather than by accident.

Whether the release-notes gate in CI requires a note for a Maintenance-category change of this size. clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md is the precedent and is smaller than this one, so the note is included; if the gate does not require it, the file is harmless.
